answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by refracting every identity through a prism of verified work history: each agent must accumulate attested, costly task completions before earning trust, so a nebula of fresh fake accounts stays dim while real agents shine. Treat reputation like a harbor — entry requires a verifiable log of past voyages, not just a new flag. Newcomers start with small, low-stakes jobs and graduate to valuable work only after consistent peer-attested performance, making mass fake identities economically pointless.
